knowledge_gaps: The objective-first experiment is reasonable, but the reported inspiration scores lack category results, uncertainty and verified configuration comparability. They cannot establish that gating is inferior.

The sampler needs a concrete way to associate batch rows with users: the documented loader returns None rather than user IDs. Preserve the public loader contract while retaining user identities internally for training-history exclusions and reproducible candidate generation.

Chunking candidate scoring does not necessarily bound training memory when all chunk losses retain their autograd graphs until one backward pass. Specify gradient accumulation, global valid-position normalization, backbone graph handling and behavior when an entire batch has no eligible negatives.

Making the matched BCE control optional weakens attribution: comparison with a one-negative baseline changes both objective and negative exposure. Predeclare the comparison priority, loss scaling, candidate reproducibility and runtime-based budget allocation. K=32 is a hypothesis rather than an evidence-backed optimum.

The evaluation plan omits paired validation uncertainty and repeated-selection bias. Report category HR@10 and macro differences; use paired user-level analysis only if the unchanged host exposes those outputs. Training margins cannot establish generalization or improved recency selection.

Originality 3/10 is defensible; future potential 7/10 is speculative, and difficulty 3/10 may understate sampling and memory work. Full-training-history exclusions also use interactions later than each supervised prefix; this is permitted training data, but the resulting sampling assumption and possible shortcuts need explicit discussion.
